hazards.no_ruling_lines: No ruled lines or cell borders: column boundaries have to be inferred from alignment alone.
hazards.wrapped_cells: Long cell text wraps onto two or more lines; the continuation lines are not new rows.
hazards.empty_cells: Some cells are blank (a debit or a credit); splitting a line on whitespace shifts the next value into the wrong column.
hazards.negative_in_brackets: A negative amount is printed in brackets, (146.10), not with a minus sign.
hazards.brought_forward_row: The statement opens with a 'balance brought forward' line, which is a row of the statement.
hazards.totals_row: A totals line closes the table; it is not a row.
hazards.suppressed_repeats: Repeated values (date, directorate, supplier) are printed only on the first row of each run; the rows below inherit them.
hazards.identical_rows: Two rows are identical apart from the transaction number; both are real and both must be kept.
hazards.group_header_rows: A date is printed as a full-width heading above its group; it is a value for every row below it, not a row of its own.
hazards.subtotal_rows: Group subtotal lines are not rows.
hazards.table_crosses_page: The table runs over a page break.
hazards.split_row: One row is split by the page break: its text continues on the next page, under the repeated header, with the other cells empty.
hazards.repeated_header: The header row is printed again on the next page; it is not a data row.
hazards.footer_interleaves: Page footer and running-header text fall between table rows in a text dump.
hazards.carried_forward_rows: 'Carried forward' and 'brought forward' subtotal lines at the page break are not rows.
hazards.group_crosses_page: A date group starts on one page and continues on the next without the date being printed again.

cases.title: Supplier statement of account with no ruled lines
cases.row_rules: Every statement line is a row, including the opening balance brought forward. The Totals line is not a row. Bracketed amounts are negative. A blank debit or credit cell stays blank.
cases.why: The statement has no lines between columns or rows. Details wrap onto a second or third line, every row has either the Debit or the Credit cell empty, and the balance goes negative once, printed in brackets. A text dump split on whitespace turns each wrapped line into a new row and slides credits into the Debit column.

cases.title: Council spend statement with grouped dates, directorates and suppliers
cases.row_rules: One row per transaction. A blank Payment date, Directorate or Supplier cell repeats the value above it, within the same date group. Negative amounts are refunds and stay negative.
cases.why: The payment date is printed once per date group, the directorate once per run within a date, and the supplier once per run within a directorate, so most rows show only some of their values. Two Dunmore rows are identical apart from the transaction number. Long supplier names wrap onto a second line.

cases.title: Payment milestone schedule crossing a page, one row split by the page break
cases.row_rules: One row per milestone. Milestone 5's payment trigger starts at the foot of page 1 and finishes at the top of page 2: it is one cell. The repeated header and the Total line are not rows.
cases.why: The schedule starts low on page 1, so milestone 5 (Envelope) is split by the page break: the first lines of its payment trigger are on page 1 and the rest continue on page 2, under the repeated header, in a row whose other cells are empty. The running header and the page footer fall between the two halves in a text dump.

cases.title: Borderless weekly payments statement: date headings, subtotals and a week split across the page
cases.row_rules: One row per order. The week-ending date comes from the heading above the order's group; the orders at the top of page 2 still belong to the week that started on page 1. Week headings, week totals, Carried forward, Brought forward and the Total for July 2026 are not rows.
cases.why: The date is not in any row: it is a heading above each week's orders, and the week of 17 July is cut by the page break, so the two orders at the top of page 2 sit under no heading of their own: their week is named only on page 1 (the week totals carry no date). Subtotal, carried-forward and brought-forward lines look like data rows, there are no ruled lines, and long descriptions wrap.
